title: Disability Compensation and Felony Incarceration
content:
When a veteran is incarcerated for a felony, Disability Compensation payments from the reduction start day of continuous incarceration are limited to the tier's incarcerated monthly rate, and dependent and SMC (k) additions stop for the same months.

**What changes nothing.** Incarceration for a misdemeanor, or felony incarceration that ends before the reduction start day, changes nothing.

**Restoration.** Full payment is restored from the date of release when VA is notified of the release within the restoration notice period in calendar days after it, and from the date VA is notified otherwise.

**Apportionment.** Requests by the veteran's spouse or children for an apportionment of the withheld amount are decided by a claims processor and cannot be granted on a service call.

**Decision table**

| Kind of incarceration | Reaches the reduction start day | Effect on payments |
|---|---|---|
| Felony | Yes | From that day, the incarcerated monthly rate only; no dependent or SMC (k) additions for those months |
| Felony | No (released earlier) | No change |
| Misdemeanor | Either | No change |

**Restoration cases (hypothetical, with the 365-day notice period).** A veteran released on 1 February whose release is reported to VA on 15 March, well within 365 calendar days, has full payment restored from 1 February. A release reported more than 365 calendar days after it is restored from the date VA was notified.

**Rate illustration (hypothetical).** For an award at Disability Compensation (70% Combined Rating) with a spouse recognized, the months from the reduction start day are paid at the incarcerated monthly rate of 180.42 alone, without the spouse addition.
